fields.expected: I'm an undergraduate at Johns Hopkins studying Applied Mathematics & Statistics and Economics, class of 2029, and most of my work has been building data and ML systems that real people use. At Summer Atlantic Capital / SAC Nexus I build the machine-learning core of an anomaly-detection and alert-prioritization system, and I own major parts of the infrastructure around it: the repository and CI scaffold, the event-ingestion pipeline, a versioned FastAPI microservice, and the public detection API. The modeling side involves temporal sequence models over event streams, anomaly scoring, and a learning-to-rank layer, plus a retrieval-augmented explanation layer so analysts can act on outputs. At Intelehealth I built a resource-availability scoring pipeline in Python across 32 villages and designed an evaluation framework comparing LLM-generated clinical outputs against a 4,169-case standard using stratified sampling. On a Gates Foundation-funded health equity project I trained XGBoost models on roughly 10 million survey records and used SHAP for feature selection. I also co-founded Open Health Intelligence and shipped ClarityAtlas, an iOS product, into a live Hopkins pilot with 30+ users.
